q: 1. The window which is provided on a sloping roof of a building, is called
explain: A dormer window is a vertical window that projects from a sloping roof, usually including its own small roof, to provide light and ventilation to an attic or top floor.

q: 2. The horizontal member spanning the window and door openings in the masonry walls is called ...........
explain: A lintel is a horizontal structural beam that spans the opening of a window or door to carry the weight of the wall above it.

q: 3. Small window is which shutters are allowed to swing around pivots fixed to the window frame
explain: A pivoted window has a sash that rotates on horizontal or vertical pivots located at the center of the frame.

q: 4. In public buildings the maximum riser is limited to
explain: Public buildings require easier ascent for diverse users; therefore, the riser is restricted to 15 cm, whereas residential buildings may allow up to 19 cm.

q: 5. The term string is used for
options: outer projecting edge of a tread
a sloping member which supports the steps in a stair
a vertical member between two treads
explain: A string (or stringer) is the sloping wooden or steel member that supports the treads and risers of a staircase.

q: 6. The vertical posts placed at the top and bottom ends of a flight supporting the hand rail are known as
explain: Newel posts are the heavy vertical posts at the start, end, or turns of a handrail system.

q: 7. Sum of tread and rise must lie between
explain: The standard comfort rule for stairs is that (Rise + Tread) should be approximately 40 to 45 cm.

q: 8. In public buildings the width of the steps may be kept between ..........
explain: Public buildings require wider stairs for mass egress, typically ranging from 1.5 m to 1.8 m.

q: 9. In a stair, when rise and going are expressed in cms, their sum should be between ..........
explain: A common rule of thumb for comfortable stair design is that the sum of the rise and the going (tread) should be approximately 40 cm to 45 cm.

q: 10. The width of rebate provided in a door frame is equal to the width of the shutter whereas depth of the rebate provided should be
explain: The rebate depth (usually 12-13 mm) is standard to ensure the door shutter sits flush and provides a seal against light and sound.

q: 11. Generally in latrines, kitchens and bathrooms the door used is from the type of
options: partly glazed and partly panelled door
explain: Flush doors are preferred for wet areas because they are easy to clean, offer no crevices for dirt or moisture, and can be easily made waterproof.

q: 12. In a residential building, the width of a door cannot be less than
explain: While internal doors for bathrooms can be 0.75m, the general standard for habitable rooms in a residential building is 0.9m to allow for furniture and occupant movement.

q: 13. Combination of king-post truss and queen post truss is used when the span is ..........
explain: For spans greater than 12 meters, combined trusses or steel trusses are used to provide adequate structural support.

q: 14. As compared to the floor area of a room, the glass area in a window should not be less than
explain: For adequate daylighting, building codes typically require the window glass area to be at least 1/10th (10%) of the floor area.

q: 15. When more lighting is required inside the buildings such as workshops and factories with fairly large spans ..........
explain: North-light roofs have a steep glazed side facing north to provide uniform, glare-free natural light into large floor areas.

q: 16. The extreme support of a hand railing provided at the top and bottom of a flight is known as
explain: A newel post is the heavy vertical post at the start or end of a stair flight that provides structural anchoring for the handrail.

q: 17. A semi-circular moulding provided on the edges of wood is known as ..........
explain: Beading is a decorative semi-circular strip or moulding used to finish edges or joints in woodwork.

q: 18. While designing a stair, the product of rise and going is approximately kept equal to
explain: One of the standard rules for comfortable stairs is (Rise in cm x Going in cm) ≈ 400 to 450. Option 420 is the most common target.

q: 19. The under surface of stair is called as
explain: The soffit refers specifically to the exposed underside of any architectural element, including stairs, arches, or cornices.

q: 20. The additional support given to the nosing in a wooden stair is known as
explain: Scotia is a concave molding placed under the nosing of a tread to strengthen the joint and provide a finished look.

q: 21. The width of stair in a residential building cannot be less than
explain: A minimum of 80cm to 90cm is required to allow for one person to comfortably ascend or carry items.

q: 22. If landing is not to be counted then the number of treads as compared to risers in a stair are
explain: In a single flight, the last step up lands on the floor level, meaning there is always one less tread than there are risers (T = R - 1).

q: 23. The door designated as 10 DT 20 means ..........
options: a single shuttered door of 1 m x 2 m
a double shuttered door of 1 m x 2 m
a single shuttered door of 2 m x 1 m
a double shuttered door of 2 m x 1 m
explain: In code designation: 10 refers to width (10 dm = 1 m), DT refers to Double Shutter, and 20 refers to height (20 dm = 2 m).

q: 24. The depression on the recess made inside the door frame to receive the shutter is called ..........
explain: A rebate is the continuous step or groove cut into the frame into which the shutter fits when closed.

q: 25. A door in which the shutter is formed by joining the vertical wooden boards side by side with tongue and grooved joints and which are fixed together by horizontal supports is called ..........
explain: Battened and ledged doors consist of vertical boards (battens) held together by horizontal members (ledges).

q: 26. The type of door used when good ventilation is required in the room and at the same time privacy is maintained ..........
explain: Louvered doors have inclined slats (louvers) that allow air to pass through while blocking the line of sight for privacy.

q: 27. A vertical window provided on the sloping roof is known as ..........
explain: A dormer window is a vertical window that projects from a sloping roof, providing light and ventilation to the attic space.

q: 28. Joining two wooden boards at an oblique angle is termed ..........
explain: Mitring involves cutting the ends of two members at an angle (usually 45°) so they form a neat corner joint, commonly used in frames.

q: 29. U-shaped pieces made of wrought iron with pointed ends which are used to connect the members are known as ..........
explain: In carpentry, 'dogs' are U-shaped iron fastners used to hold large timber members together during construction or in heavy trusses.

q: 30. A window provided on a pitched roof parallel and slightly above the sloping roof surface is known as ..........
explain: Unlike a dormer, a sky light is installed parallel to the roof slope to bring natural light directly into the room below.

q: 31. The members laid horizontally to support the common rafters and to transmit the load to the trusses walls are called as
explain: Purlins are horizontal beams that span between trusses to support the roof rafters or sheeting.

q: 32. For a span ranging in between 6 m to 9 m, the most suitable type of pitched roof is
explain: The King Post truss is the most efficient design for spans up to 9 meters.

q: 33. The normal tread length varies between
explain: A tread length (going) of 25cm to 30cm ensures the full foot has enough surface area to land safely.

q: 34. The horizontal members of the shutter of a door or window are called
explain: Rails are the horizontal structural members of a shutter, such as top, lock, and bottom rails.

q: 35. In wooden stairs the thickness of the member used as tread is generally ..........
explain: To provide sufficient structural strength for foot traffic, the horizontal part of the step (tread) in timber stairs is usually 38 mm thick.

q: 36. While the depth of the rebate equals the thickness of the door shutter, the width of the rebate is usually ..........
explain: The rebate depth matches the door thickness (e.g., 30-40mm), but the width (the overlap) is usually about 12 mm.

q: 37. The most suitable type of door for air-conditioned rooms ..........
explain: Revolving doors minimize the exchange of air between the interior and exterior, making them highly efficient for climate control.

q: 38. The number of steps in an ordinary flight shall not be more than ..........
explain: A flight is generally limited to 12 steps to prevent excessive fatigue for the user before reaching a landing.

q: 39. In a stair, the ratio of the vertical distance covered to the horizontal distance occupied by the flight is called ..........
explain: The pitch (or slope) of a stair is the angle between the line of nosings and the horizontal plane.

q: 40. The angle which the line of nosing of the stair makes with the horizontal, is called ..........
explain: The pitch is the angle of inclination of the stairs, ideally between 25 and 40 degrees.

q: 41. In residential building, the average value of stair width is ..........
explain: A minimum width of 900mm (0.9m) is standard for residential stairs to allow for a single person to move comfortably.

q: 42. The pitch of stair should never exceed ..........
explain: Stairs steeper than 40 degrees are difficult to climb and become dangerous; they are typically kept between 25° and 40°.

q: 43. A horizontal member of a frame employed to sub-divide a window opening horizontally is called ..........
explain: A transom is a horizontal bar of wood or stone across a window or door.

q: 44. The depth of jambs is ..........
explain: The depth of the jamb or frame section is usually between 60mm and 75mm.

q: 45. The window used with the object of providing light and air to the end closed space below the roof is called ..........
explain: A dormer window is a vertical window that projects from a sloping roof.

q: 46. The horizontal members of wood or steel used to support the common rafter of a sloping roof, are called ..........
explain: Purlins are horizontal structural members that span between trusses or walls to support the common rafters or roofing sheets.

q: 47. The term pitch in connection with pitched roofs is defined as a ..........
options: apex line of the sloping roof
inclination of the sides of a roof to the horizontal plane
horizontal distance between the internal faces of the walls
triangular upper part of a wall formed at the end of a pitch roof
explain: Pitch is the numerical measure of the steepness of a roof, expressed as the ratio of rise to span or as an angle.

q: 48. Keeping in view possibility of shrinkage and wrapping the width of the boards is recommended to be ...........
explain: Narrower boards (approx. 10 cm) are less prone to significant warping or 'cupping' compared to wider boards.
